rationales.quote: Does it change in real time?
rationales.explanation: Asks whether the proposed pricing solution operates dynamically in real time.

rationales.quote: So do you integrate with their POS?
rationales.explanation: Tests whether the solution can connect to restaurants’ point-of-sale systems.

rationales.quote: Is that a signed deal?
rationales.explanation: Checks whether the key white-label integration relationship is contractually secured.

rationales.quote: And what are they doing for you?
rationales.explanation: Seeks to understand the partner’s operational role in delivering the solution.

rationales.quote: $99 a month seems very low to me for an enterprise SAAS solution.
rationales.explanation: Raises concern that the proposed enterprise SaaS price may under-monetize the product.

rationales.quote: How’d you come up with that pricing?
rationales.explanation: Requests the basis for the proposed pricing model.

rationales.quote: Who on your team has that experience of enterprise SAAS sales?
rationales.explanation: Probes whether the team has relevant enterprise SaaS sales capability.

rationales.quote: You're doing it at an earlier stage, which is great.
rationales.explanation: Views the early pivot, despite initial traction, as evidence of timely execution judgment.

rationales.quote: You're the real deal.
rationales.explanation: Explicitly cites a strong overall impression of the founder as a reason to invest.

rationales.quote: you have a clear vision for the business and for the future of restaurant pricing
rationales.explanation: Supports investment based on the founder’s clear direction for the company and category.

rationales.quote: You know the industry, you know the pain point.
rationales.explanation: Cites the founder’s market knowledge and understanding of the customer problem as investment reasons.

rationales.quote: you're smart enough to be pivoting at an early stage
rationales.explanation: Explicitly treats the early pivot as evidence of sound execution judgment.

rationales.quote: I think the round is priced very fairly, even though you're early.
rationales.explanation: Supports investment because the financing price is viewed as fair for the company’s early stage.

rationales.quote: Just do A/B testing, that's all! Simple A/B testing.
rationales.explanation: Identifies straightforward A/B testing as a sufficient practical product approach.

post-pitch interviews, later diligence and subsequent updates; teaser is an opening preview/repeated future clip. Use unclear

reversals stay original_pitch. Immediate investor-only debrief in the same room after the founder exits also stays
original_pitch; it is NOT later_commentary. Reserve later_commentary for separate interviews, diligence or updates. Do not mix retrospective opinions into original-pitch scoring.

merely any question. decision_link supports_in/out ONLY if the target links the rationale to the commitment/refusal.
Confidence concerns the annotation, not investment probability. Return reviewed_target_turns containing EVERY supplied target
turn index exactly once, even when it contains no rationale. An empty rationale list is valid if none was expressed.
Be concise: prefer one short exact quote per distinct concept/turn, and a one-sentence explanation. Never claim human validation.
